sections.h2: Where does a Pitt County deed get recorded?
sections.html:
A deed for Pitt County land is recorded at the Pitt County Register of Deeds, at 100 E. 1st Street in Greenville. The county page lists office hours of 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m., Monday through Friday, and a phone line at 252-902-1650.

The same office keeps deeds, deeds of trust, easements, plats and the other land papers that make up the chain of title. Some of the records go back to the 1700s, since Pitt County was formed in 1760. For a seller, the office matters at one moment above all: the deed that moves the house to a buyer has to land in these books before it protects anyone.

sections.h2: Why does recording order matter when selling a Pitt County house?
sections.html:
Because North Carolina protects the buyer who records first. Under G.S. 47-18, a conveyance, option or longer lease does not hold up against lien creditors or paying purchasers until it is registered in the county where the land sits, and priority follows the time of registration.

For a Pitt County sale, that explains why closings end with a recording step and why buyers and title agents care about the time stamp. A deed signed but left in a drawer protects nobody. If you hold an old unrecorded deed, for example from a family transfer, record it or talk to a closing attorney before you list or sign a contract.

sections.h2: What does it cost to record in Pitt County?
sections.html:
Fees are set by the General Assembly and the county page says they are the same in every county. The Pitt County fee summary lists these items:

  • General instruments such as deeds and easements: $26 for the first 15 pages and $4 for each extra page.
  • Plats: $21 per sheet.
  • Non-standard document: $25 added to the base fee.
  • Several instruments filed together: $10 for each additional one.
  • Certified copy of a recorded document: $5 for the first page and $2 for each extra page.
  • Satisfaction or cancellation of a mortgage or deed of trust: no charge.

The county's summary lists mortgages and deeds of trust at $56 for the first 15 pages, while the current text of G.S. 161-10 prints $64 for the first 35 pages. Call the office before you send a lender document so the check matches. Payment can be cash, check, money order or a card.

sections.h2: How much is the transfer tax on a Pitt County sale?
sections.html:
The excise tax is $1.00 for each $500, or part of $500, of the price. The Pitt County records page says it is based on the sale price and paid when the deed is recorded.

The statute, G.S. 105-228.30, puts the duty on the transferor, meaning the seller, and requires payment to the register of deeds before recording. Half goes to the county general fund and half to the State. Your closing statement will show the line; ask the closing attorney to confirm it before signing.

sections.h2: Can I record a deed electronically in Pitt County?
sections.html:
Yes. The county says it accepts electronic recordings through several vendors and tells filers to contact each one to compare prices. The vendors named on the county page are Corporation Service Company, eRecording Partners Network, Indecomm Global Services and Simplifile.

Most sellers never deal with this step. A title company or closing attorney usually submits the deed and the buyer's deed of trust together. Still, if you are handling a family transfer without a lender, ask whether your preparer files by e-recording or in person, and who pays the vendor charge.

sections.h2: How can a Pitt County owner watch for deed fraud and check records?
sections.html:
Pitt County offers an alert sign-up so owners are told when a document is recorded under their name or property. The county also runs an online search for recorded documents from September 1762 to the present, searchable by grantor, grantee, document type, book and page, or date range.

  • Search the grantor index for your name to see every recorded deed or lien tied to you.
  • Use book and page numbers from an old deed to pull the full document.
  • Use the county's Online Parcel Information System, run by Tax Administration and GIS, to view parcel boundaries, assessed values, tax districts and flood zones.
  • Older index books can be used on site at the Greenville office.

Run this check before you list a house, especially an inherited one. An unreleased deed of trust or a missing link in the title is far easier to fix before a buyer is waiting.

sections.h2: What other papers might a Pitt County sale involve?
sections.html:
Beyond the deed, a Pitt County closing can include a deed of trust for the buyer's loan, a recorded release of the seller's old loan, and sometimes a plat or easement. Each one is filed separately and priced under the fee list above.

  • Old loan: confirm the lender recorded a satisfaction.
  • New loan: the buyer's lender records its own deed of trust.
  • Seller financing: see the contract for deed rules in Chapter 47H, which call for recording within five business days.

The county's FAQ lists agreements, assignments, assumed names, leases and subdivision maps among the land-related documents the office records.

sections.h2: What should a Pitt County seller do before closing?
sections.html:
Start with a title check, then line up the paperwork a closing attorney will need. Pull the vesting deed, confirm every deed of trust has a recorded satisfaction, and ask the tax office about the current bill.

Property tax is a separate office from the register of deeds. North Carolina taxes are due September 1 and carry interest if unpaid after January 5, which G.S. 105-360 describes as 2 percent for January and three-fourths of one percent each month after. When a Pitt County house sells, ask the closing attorney how the current year's bill will be handled at the table. The tax office, not this page, gives the balance.

If the house needs work, has tenants or sits in an estate, a direct cash buyer can close on a short timeline and the same recording steps apply. Whoever buys, the deed still goes to the Greenville office.

faqs.q: Where is the Pitt County Register of Deeds?
faqs.a: It is at 100 E. 1st Street, Greenville, NC 27834, open Monday through Friday from 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m., per the county page. The phone number listed is 252-902-1650.

faqs.q: Who pays the excise tax on a Pitt County sale?
faqs.a: The seller pays. G.S. 105-228.30 makes the transferor responsible, and the tax is collected at recording at $1.00 for each $500 of value. Your closing statement should show it.

faqs.q: Does Pitt County charge to record a mortgage satisfaction?
faqs.a: No. The county fee summary lists satisfactions and cancellations of mortgages and deeds of trust as no charge. A lender is still the party that files the release, so ask yours to record it.

faqs.q: Can I search Pitt County deeds from home?
faqs.a: Yes. The county says recorded real estate documents from September 1762 to the present are searchable online by name, document type, book and page, or date range.

faqs.q: What are the fees for recording a deed in Pitt County?
faqs.a: The county lists $26 for the first 15 pages of a general instrument plus $4 per extra page. Plats are $21 per sheet. Call the office to confirm the total for your document, including any non-standard document charge.
